packages.label: תְּפִלָּה בִּדְבֵקוּת וּשְׁגִירַת הַפֶּה
packages.label_en: Prayer with Devekut and Fluency of the Mouth
packages.reason: The single bechina equation in Torah #99 links two expressions of the same spiritual quality: prayer conducted with devekut (attachment to God) and the experience of prayer being שְׁגוּרָה בְּפִיו — fluent, flowing, and easily articulated in one's mouth. The Rebbe cites Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's rule (Berakhot 34b): when his prayer was fluent in his mouth he knew it was accepted; when not, he knew it was not. The Rebbe interprets this as a single bechina: fluency of prayer IS devekut, and devekut IS fluency of prayer. They are two faces of the same inner state — the condition in which the soul's attachment to God expresses itself as words that pour forth naturally and freely from the mouth. Neither produces the other; they are the same reality seen from two angles: the inner spiritual state (devekut) and its outer linguistic expression (shlimut/shgura). Both nodes are positive, belonging to the domain of authentic prayer and cleaving to God.
